w: Ependymoma arises from the ependymal lining, often in the fourth ventricle, but the classic cerebellar small-blue-cell tumor of childhood is medulloblastoma.
Pilocytic astrocytoma is a cystic, slow-growing cerebellar tumor with Rosenthal fibers, usually less aggressive.
p: Medulloblastoma is the most common malignant pediatric brain tumor: midline cerebellar vermis mass causing obstructive hydrocephalus; small round blue cells with Homer Wright rosettes.

w: Nafcillin treats methicillin-sensitive staphylococci, not Neisseria gonorrhoeae.
Vancomycin covers resistant gram-positive cocci and has no role for gram-negative diplococci.
p: Gonococcal arthritis is treated with ceftriaxone plus joint aspiration or drainage; consider azithromycin or doxycycline for possible chlamydia.

w: Cholangiocarcinoma is linked to liver flukes and primary sclerosing cholangitis, not alpha-1 antitrypsin deficiency.
Angiosarcoma follows vinyl chloride or arsenic exposure rather than alpha-1 antitrypsin deficiency.
p: Alpha-1 antitrypsin deficiency causes panacinar emphysema (lower lobes) and liver cirrhosis, which raises the risk of hepatocellular carcinoma.

bw: No response to olanzapine, quetiapine, risperidone
w: Haloperidol is a first-generation antipsychotic with no proven advantage after failed second-generation drugs.
Aripiprazole is another second-generation agent; treatment resistance after 2 adequate trials points to clozapine.
p: Treatment-resistant schizophrenia (two failed adequate trials) is the indication for clozapine; monitor for agranulocytosis, seizures and myocarditis.

bw: Painful defecation, bright red blood on stool
w: Curettage of a tract is for pilonidal or fistula disease, not a fissure.
Colonoscopy is not needed first for a classic fissure in a young patient with no alarm features.
p: Anal fissures heal with fiber, sitz baths and topical calcium channel blockers or nitroglycerin; botulinum toxin and sphincterotomy are for refractory cases.

w: Neurofibrillary tangles with tau characterize Alzheimer disease, which declines gradually rather than stepwise.
Lewy bodies mark Lewy body dementia with hallucinations and parkinsonism.
p: Vascular dementia follows small-vessel disease and infarcts, giving stepwise decline with focal signs and gait changes.

bw: No urine for 6 hours after thyroidectomy
w: Renal biopsy is invasive and reserved for unexplained intrinsic kidney disease.
Furosemide would not help before excluding urinary retention and hypovolemia.
p: Postoperative anuria is most often urinary retention (anesthesia, opioids); a bladder scan is noninvasive and quick before further workup.

bw: Provoked bite by a neighbor's dog
w: Euthanasia and testing are for stray or unavailable animals that cannot be observed.
Immune globulin and vaccine are started only if the healthy dog develops signs during observation.
p: A healthy domestic dog or cat that bites is quarantined and observed for 10 days; prophylaxis starts only if it becomes ill.

bw: Stocking sensory loss, absent ankle jerks
w: Lumbar puncture helps in Guillain-Barre or CNS infection but does not characterize a chronic distal neuropathy.
Brain MRI would not explain distal symmetric lower-limb signs.
p: EMG with nerve conduction studies distinguishes axonal from demyelinating neuropathy and localizes the lesion.

bw: No response after 8 weeks of first-line drug
w: Propranolol treats performance anxiety and tremor but does not augment SSRIs in OCD.
Phenelzine is an MAOI, risky with serotonergic drugs, and not an augmentation agent.
p: SSRI-resistant OCD is augmented with low-dose antipsychotics such as risperidone or aripiprazole; clomipramine is an alternative.

bw: Stiff neck, afebrile, no focal deficit
w: Lumbar puncture follows a negative CT (xanthochromia) and is not the first test.
MRI is slower and less sensitive than CT for acute subarachnoid blood in the first hours.
p: Suspected subarachnoid hemorrhage needs an immediate noncontrast head CT, then lumbar puncture if negative and suspicion remains.

w: Condylomata are warty papules from HPV, not a soft cystic swelling.
A vulvar hematoma follows trauma and is acutely tender and bruised.
p: Bartholin duct obstruction produces a cyst at 4 or 8 o'clock; infected cysts form abscesses needing drainage.

w: Dextroamphetamine is another stimulant and would cause the same appetite suppression.
Imipramine is a tricyclic reserved for refractory cases and has more adverse effects.
p: Atomoxetine, a selective norepinephrine reuptake inhibitor, is a non-stimulant alternative when stimulants are not tolerated.

w: Ergonovine is an ergot vasoconstrictor and would worsen nausea.
Propranolol is migraine prophylaxis, not an antiemetic.
p: Dopamine antagonists (chlorpromazine, metoclopramide, prochlorperazine) relieve migraine pain and nausea.

bw: Sudden right arm and face weakness, slurred speech
w: Carotid stenosis is shown on duplex ultrasound and would not explain the ECG question.
Intraparenchymal hyperdensity is a CT finding of hemorrhage, not an ECG finding.
p: Cardioembolic stroke from atrial fibrillation is sudden with cortical signs; hyperthyroidism is a common AF trigger.

w: Secondary prophylaxis with valve disease lasts at least 10 years or until about age 40, so stopping at 25 is too early.
Cefotaxime is not the standard agent; penicillin G remains first line.
p: Secondary prophylaxis after rheumatic fever with residual valve disease continues for at least 10 years since the last attack or until age 40.
